title: My dear One
line: Five days of greeting the One in every irritation.
intro: Immanence, Athena says, means recognising the One in everything, including what annoys us: at the tax office, on the road, in a heated debate. Life, in Athena’s reading, is divine play in which the One plays every role. For five days, greet the One in every irritation and tell yourself, “one more game”.
does: Silently greet the One in each irritation, say “one more game”, and count them at night.
trains: Seeing the One in what annoys you, and playing your part without being caught in it.
each: Whenever something irritates you (a queue, a driver who cuts in, a heated meeting, a slow reply), silently greet the One there, “my dear One”, and tell yourself, “one more game”. Keep a rough count as you go, on your fingers or in a note, and at night count them.
note: How many did you count today, and which one was hardest to greet?
end: After five days: has anything changed in how irritation arrives, or in how long it stays?
